best-broadway-shows.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows: March 2026

Broadway enters spring 2026 with a remarkably strong lineup that balances groundbreaking new work with beloved revivals. This month's top ten shows average an impressive 83 out of 100 from critics, reflecting a season where artistic ambition meets consistent execution.

**Hamilton** continues its reign as Broadway's most acclaimed production, with critics still celebrating Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop reimagining of American history as a revolutionary theatrical achievement. The show's sustained excellence nearly a decade into its run demonstrates its lasting impact on the art form.

Among newer productions, **Maybe Happy Ending** emerges as a critical darling, earning praise as one of Broadway's most original musicals in years. This charming robot love story proves that inventive storytelling can still find fresh ground on Broadway. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!**—Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a boozy, cabaret-obsessed narcissist—delivers the kind of irreverent comedy that has critics and audiences roaring with laughter.

The season also showcases Broadway's ability to keep classic productions vital. **The Lion King** remains a stunning achievement in theatrical craft, while **Ragtime**'s revival resonates with particular timeliness. **The Book of Mormon** and **Chicago** continue to prove their enduring appeal, and **Hadestown**'s folk-opera approach to Greek mythology still captivates audiences. Rounding out the list, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** dazzles with technical wizardry, and **Buena Vista Social Club** transports audiences with intoxicating Cuban rhythms.

Whether you're drawn to innovative new voices or timeless spectacle, this month's Broadway offerings provide compelling options across every theatrical taste.

# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted. That season's brief window before the pandemic shutdown produced a diverse slate of productions—from bold reimaginings of classics to powerful dramatic revivals—that continue to resonate with audiences today.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which earns an 83/100 critic score for its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This fresh take on the beloved musical demonstrates how even well-worn material can find new life through reimagined staging, though the approach doesn't convince all critics.

**A Soldier's Play** stands out as perhaps the season's most significant dramatic achievement, scoring 78/100 across 29 reviews. Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning work finally received its long-overdue Broadway debut in a stellar revival that proves the play's examination of race, power, and identity remains urgently relevant decades after it was written.

The season also featured notable experiments in form and interpretation. Laura Linney's solo performance in **My Name is Lucy Barton** divides critics but showcases the actor's luminous talents, while Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves polarizing—some embrace its visceral, video-enhanced approach while others find it at odds with the material's essence.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the class of 2020 represents a solid, if uneven, theatrical moment—one that mixed respectful revivals with adventurous reinterpretations. For those exploring what remains of this abbreviated season, these productions offer varied entry points into Broadway's last pre-pandemic chapter.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back in March 2026 at the Broadway plays that opened in 2020, we're examining a season dramatically cut short by the pandemic—yet one that still managed to deliver several noteworthy productions before the shutdown.

Among the five plays that premiered during this truncated season, a refurbished **Les Misérables** at the Sondheim Theatre leads our rankings with an 83/100 critic score. This grittier reboot of the classic production earns praise from most reviewers, though its darker approach doesn't win over everyone. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** (78/100) marks a powerful, long-overdue Broadway debut for Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama, with critics applauding a stellar revival that demonstrates the work's enduring relevance to contemporary audiences.

The season also features **My Name is Lucy Barton** (71/100), a solo adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel that divides critics despite widespread acclaim for Laura Linney's luminous performance. Bess Wohl's **Grand Horizons** (71/100) receives similar marks as a pleasant if familiar boulevard comedy elevated by strong performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Rounding out the list, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining (68/100) proves the season's most polarizing production, with critics split between those who embrace its bold vision and those who find the experimental approach misguided.

With an average critic score of 74/100 across these five productions, the abbreviated 2020 season demonstrates both artistic ambition and the resilience of works that tackle enduring themes. Explore our detailed reviews to discover which of these productions aligns with your theatrical tastes.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that premiered in 2021 represent a remarkable period of artistic renewal and experimentation. That year marked the industry's tentative reopening after an unprecedented shutdown, and the productions that emerged reflect both the hunger for theatrical innovation and the enduring appeal of Broadway spectacle.

The highest-rated production from this cohort is **Dana H.**, an unconventional docudrama that continues to captivate audiences with Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance. Critics describe it as unforgettable—a bold experiment in theatrical form that pushes the boundaries of what drama can be. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** stands as an epic achievement, transforming 150 years of American capitalism into gripping theater through extraordinary performances and stunning direction. And **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club** demonstrates how radical reimagining can breathe new life into classic material, with Rebecca Frecknall's immersive production earning acclaim for its complete transformation of the Playhouse Theatre.

The ten productions featured here average an impressive 81/100 critical score, spanning from intimate solo performances like **Lackawanna Blues** to the spectacular return of **The Phantom of the Opera**, from verbatim documentary theater in **Is This a Room** to the pop exuberance of **SIX**. Together, they showcase Broadway's remarkable range—its capacity for both experimental risk-taking and crowd-pleasing entertainment, often within the same season.

Whether you're seeking challenging theatrical innovation or beloved musical spectacle, these productions from 2021's reopening season offer compelling options for today's theatergoers.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands as a remarkable period of theatrical achievement, with an exceptional concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning works and critically acclaimed revivals that continue to resonate with audiences.

The season's crown jewel is **Kimberly Akimbo**, David Lindsay-Abaire and Jeanine Tesori's musical about a teenager with a rare aging condition. Critics consistently praise its delicate balance of quirky humor and emotional depth, earning it the highest marks of the year. Close behind are two equally impressive productions: **Into the Woods**, a stripped-down Sondheim revival that serves as a fitting tribute to the late composer, and **A Strange Loop**, Michael R. Jackson's brazenly original meta-musical that took home the Pulitzer Prize for Drama.

What distinguishes 2022 is the remarkable quality across the board—the ten featured shows average an impressive 83/100 critic score. The season showcases an unusual number of Pulitzer winners, including Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog**, Tom Stoppard's deeply personal **Leopoldstadt**, Stephen Adly Guirgis's **Between Riverside and Crazy**, Paula Vogel's **How I Learned to Drive**, and Martyna Majok's **Cost of Living**. This concentration of award-winning drama alongside innovative new work like Jordan E. Cooper's audacious satire **Ain't No Mo'** and Mike Birbiglia's masterful solo show creates a season that exemplifies Broadway's capacity for both entertainment and profound artistic expression.

Whether you're catching these productions during their runs or exploring recordings and future revivals, these ten shows represent essential viewing for anyone interested in contemporary American theater.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2023

As of March 2026, the Broadway plays that premiered in 2023 continue to demonstrate the enduring power of theatrical storytelling, with an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across our top ten selections.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's revelatory revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which has successfully transformed Sondheim's infamous 1981 flop into a critical triumph. The production earns an 85/100 rating, matching the score of **Stranger Things: The First Shadow**, a West End transfer that has surprised critics by transcending its pop culture origins to deliver technically stunning, standalone theatre. Close behind, **Appropriate** has established itself as essential viewing, with Sarah Paulson anchoring what critics call a modern masterpiece of family dysfunction and buried secrets.

The 2023 season notably balanced artistic ambition with cultural urgency. **Purlie Victorious** brought Ossie Davis's 1961 satire back to Broadway with striking contemporary resonance, while **Parade** found new relevance in its historical examination of prejudice and injustice. Solo performances also made their mark, with **Just for Us** demonstrating the continued vitality of one-person shows in an era of theatrical spectacle.

What distinguishes this crop of plays is their range—from intimate character studies to sprawling ensemble pieces, from sharp-edged comedy to wrenching drama. Productions like **Fat Ham**, **Sweeney Todd**, and the slow-burning critical favorite **Stereophonic** round out a season that showcased Broadway's capacity for both artistic innovation and powerful revivals.

Whether you're seeking Sondheim's redemption, Pulitzer-winning innovation, or searing contemporary drama, these 2023 productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theatre at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in 2024

As we look back from March 2026, the 2024 Broadway season stands out as a remarkably diverse year that brought fresh voices and bold revivals to the stage. From intimate character studies to sprawling rock epics, these productions demonstrate the range and vitality of contemporary theater.

Leading our rankings is **La Llamada**, though with limited critical coverage thus far. Close behind, **Stereophonic** emerges as the season's most discussed achievement—David Adjmi's meticulous recreation of a 1970s rock band's creative process has captivated critics with its authentic portrayal of artistic collaboration and the cost of making music. The production's attention to period detail and emotional nuance has earned it recognition as a theatrical landmark.

Musical theater innovation thrives in **Maybe Happy Ending**, a robot love story that critics celebrate as one of Broadway's most original offerings in recent memory, and **Operation Mincemeat**, a grassroots sensation whose inventive energy propelled it from fringe success to West End acclaim and finally to Broadway.

Comedy finds its sharpest edge in **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's absurdist reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed, wine-soaked narcissist—a performance that has critics praising its fearless irreverence. Meanwhile, classic revivals like George Wolfe's **Gypsy**, featuring Audra McDonald's deeply personal interpretation of Mama Rose, prove that canonical works still have new stories to tell.

With an average critic score of 85/100 across these ten productions, the 2024 season represents a high-water mark for quality and ambition. Whether you're drawn to experimental dance-theater, intimate drama, or reimagined classics, these shows offer compelling reasons to experience live theater at its finest.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays

As March 2026 arrives, Broadway's 2025 play season continues to resonate with audiences, offering a compelling mix of bold revivals and ambitious new works that reflect our current moment.

Leading the field is Ivo van Hove's stripped-down production of **All My Sons**, which earns the highest marks for transforming Arthur Miller's classic into a viscerally emotional experience through minimalist staging and powerhouse ensemble work. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** proves that great writing transcends time, with critics celebrating its perfect balance of humor and heart.

The season's range is remarkable: **Paddington The Musical** enchants with technical wizardry and family-friendly charm, while Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer winner **English** offers a nuanced examination of language and identity. New American plays dominate the conversation, with Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's **Purpose** and Hannah Wohl's **Liberation** delivering the sharp social commentary and complex family dynamics that define contemporary playwriting. Meanwhile, classic musicals find renewed relevance—**Ragtime** resonates powerfully in today's political climate, anchored by Joshua Henry's celebrated performance.

The unconventional also finds its place: **Dead Outlaw** brings dark comedy and rock music to the bizarre true story of Elmer McCurdy, proving Broadway's appetite for original, offbeat narratives remains strong.

With an average critic score of 84/100 across these ten productions, the 2025 play season demonstrates Broadway's continued vitality in balancing artistic ambition with accessibility. Whether you're drawn to reimagined classics, innovative new voices, or theatrical spectacle, these productions offer compelling reasons to experience live theater this spring.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

As March 2026 unfolds, the Broadway season presents a modest slate of new theatrical offerings, with critics taking measure of the year's early arrivals.

The most notable opening thus far is **Every Brilliant Thing**, which receives a mixed critical reception with a score of 66/100. The production brings its intimate exploration of mental health and human resilience to Broadway audiences, though reviews suggest the show generates more contemplation than consensus among theater critics.

With only one new play debuting so far this year, the 2026 season is still in its nascent stages. The average critical score of 66/100 reflects a theatrical landscape where productions are meeting competent standards without yet achieving the breakthrough acclaim that defines exceptional seasons. This measured start leaves considerable room for the season to evolve as more productions announce opening dates in the coming months.

The current theatrical environment appears to be one of cautious programming, with producers perhaps waiting to gauge audience appetites and economic conditions before committing major productions to Broadway houses. While **Every Brilliant Thing** offers theatergoers a worthwhile option for serious contemporary drama, the limited selection means audiences seeking variety may need to look toward revivals, long-running productions from previous seasons, or Off-Broadway venues to round out their theater calendars.

For those planning their Broadway outings in the weeks ahead, monitoring announcements for spring and summer openings will be essential to discovering what additional productions may shape the year's theatrical conversation.
